deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes Euler's practical rule (§§109–112) for the height of a vertical fountain jet fed through a long pipe in which the water suffers friction. The preceding pages derive v = (g/(αb))·(q − αbl/g)·(1 − e^{−αb/g}). Here b is the pipe length, q is the head of the reservoir (castellum) above the orifice, v is the height due to the outflow velocity, and the friction coefficient was fitted from experiment as g/α ≈ 4000 d, with d the pipe diameter.

With n = b/d and x = n/4000 the rule becomes v = Nq − M, where N = (1 − e^{−x})/x = 1 − x/2 + x²/6 − … and M is proportional to N·n. The step-by-step procedure is:
1. Divide the pipe length by its diameter to get n.
2. Read off N and M.
3. Multiply N by the head q in feet.
4. Subtract M; the remainder is the jet height in feet.

In §111 Euler states that this gives the height due to the efflux velocity, not the actual jet height. Air resistance lowers a vertical jet somewhat further, and he deliberately sets that effect aside as having a different origin.

In §112 he proposes tabulating N and M against n so that the computation is effortless; the table follows on p. 382. Checking it: N(100) = (1 − e^{−0.025})/0.025 = 0.98760 and N(4000) = 1 − 1/e = 0.6321, both correct. The tabulated M equals 3Nn/400, e.g. 0.9876·100·3/400 = 0.7407 and 0.6321·4000·3/400 = 18.963.
errors: The tabulated M (next page) equals 3Nn/400, whereas §109 on the previous page, as transcribed, gives M = Nn/400. Either the printed formula or the transcription drops a factor 3 (i.e. αl/g should correspond to 3/400 ft per unit n), or the table uses a different constant from the stated rule. This is a factor-3 inconsistency between the rule and the table.

The constant g/α = 4000d is an empirical fit to a single dataset. The friction model (resistance proportional to length with an exponential head factor) does not reproduce the later Chézy/Darcy–Weisbach dependence on velocity squared and diameter, so the rule has limited physical validity. This is a physical limitation rather than a logical error.

ideas.what: Jet height = height due to efflux velocity; air resistance treated as a separate, neglected correction
ideas.modern_name: Velocity head v²/2g versus actual jet rise (Mariotte-type air-resistance correction)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Torricelli; Mariotte (empirical fountain-height losses); Daniel Bernoulli, Hydrodynamica (1738)
ideas.where_published: E260 and Euler's other hydraulic papers on fountains and pipes (e.g. E206 on the Sanssouci-era fountain problem; uncertain on exact number)

ideas.what: Reduction of the pipe-flow solution to a two-coefficient linear rule v = Nq − M, with N = (1 − e^{−n/4000})/(n/4000), tabulated against the slenderness ratio n = L/d
ideas.modern_name: Head-loss table as a function of L/d (precursor of friction-loss charts)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Chézy (1770s), Prony, Darcy–Weisbach (1840s–50s) for pipe-friction loss formulas
ideas.where_published: E260, §§108–112 and the table on p. 382

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a practical summary of a rule plus a remark that air resistance is neglected; it contains nothing new beyond the known content of E260. The only point of interest is the factor-3 mismatch between the stated M formula and the table.
